edit.description: the constructor's `?? 4`, where the embedder's width is bound unread, and the option's hover text, which states the default and the fallback but no bound
the construction refusal, beside the wave-width cases

summary: a dispatcher constructed with a `maxParallel` below one refuses, rather than running every wave of the run as a quiet no-op over a ready queue
acceptance: constructing a `Dispatcher` with a `maxParallel` of zero, a negative, or a fraction refuses, naming the field and what omitting it defaults to, the way the chain load already refuses the declared half; an omitted option still binds four and a wave still opens four slots
tests: a dispatcher constructed with a maxParallel below one refuses
a dispatcher constructed with a fractional maxParallel refuses
pins: a dispatcher constructed with no maxParallel opens four slots

interface.changes: `new Dispatcher({ maxParallel })` refuses a width below one or a fractional one at construction, where it bound the value and ran
interface.hides: which half of the width the engine checks — an embedder no longer reads the chain-load roster to learn that its own knob is the unguarded one
interface.rejected: clamping to one, the silent degradation the declared half's refusal already turned down: an embedder that asked for no slots and got one reads as a correct wave

notes: `this.maxParallel = opts.maxParallel ?? 4` (`src/Dispatcher.ts`) binds it unread, and selection prefers it only where the chain declared nothing (`src/selection.ts`), so an embedder's 0 reaches `while (inFlight.size < maxParallel)` and the wave opens no slot. The chain-load roster's own comment already names this as the undeclared fallback (`src/chainLoad.ts`). `maxTicks` has the same split and already throws; `mergeBatch` has no embedder knob.
